priorStories.headline: U.S. sends third carrier toward Middle East
priorStories.body:
The U.S. military began sending about 9,000 sailors and Marines to the Middle East aboard the USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier strike group and the USS Makin Island amphibious readiness group, according to a U.S. official.

Their arrival could bring the regional U.S. presence to three aircraft carriers and more than 20,000 sailors and Marines.

candidates.summary: A spokesperson for Yemen’s internationally recognized government said its warplanes carried out 20 strikes over a three-hour period against Houthi movements, personnel, vehicles and military equipment in Taiz province. A Houthi military source quoted by the Houthi-run Saba news agency denied the government’s account. Reuters said roads into the province had been designated military operational areas amid wider fighting.
candidates.title: Yemeni government claims 20 airstrikes against Houthi targets in Taiz

candidates.summary: The United Nations Food and Agriculture Organization reported that its global food price index rose in September to its highest level in nearly four years. Reuters attributed the increase to weather concerns and disruptions affecting crop-market logistics. FAO had scheduled the September index for release on October 2.
candidates.title: UN global food price index reaches nearly four-year high

candidates.summary: FlyDubai captain Smit Machchhar, speaking from a hospital during a televised call with Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, described regaining his footing and opening the cockpit door during the September 30 attack aboard a Dubai-to-Tel Aviv flight. The target-day interview provided his first detailed public account of how passengers gained access to the cockpit and restrained the co-pilot accused of attacking him.
candidates.title: FlyDubai captain gives first detailed account of cockpit attack
candidates.geography: India / United Arab Emirates / Saudi Arabia

candidates.summary: The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that nonfarm payroll employment increased by 29,000 in September while the unemployment rate was 4.2%. July and August payroll gains were revised down by a combined 60,000, and average hourly earnings were 3.0% higher than a year earlier.
candidates.title: U.S. payroll growth slows to 29,000 in September

candidates.summary: G7 leaders agreed to coordinate the release of 100 million barrels of oil and fuel products through the International Energy Agency over four months, beginning immediately. Their statement called for a substantial, front-loaded diesel release during the first 20 days and said members would refrain from restricting energy exports to one another.
candidates.title: G7 agrees to coordinated release of 100 million barrels of oil and fuel

candidates.summary: Russian aerial attacks forced the full or partial closure of three of Kyiv’s six road bridges across the Dnipro River, according to Mayor Vitalii Klitschko. One bridge was struck again Friday afternoon. The closures caused major traffic disruption in the Ukrainian capital.
candidates.title: Russian attacks force closures of three Kyiv bridges

candidates.summary: Israel and the United Arab Emirates agreed to begin repatriation flights for travelers stranded after the UAE suspended commercial flights to Israel following the September 30 FlyDubai cockpit attack. Tel Aviv’s Ben Gurion Airport listed Arkia and Israir arrivals from Dubai for late Friday and early Saturday, with an El Al flight expected Sunday.
candidates.title: Israel and UAE arrange repatriation flights after FlyDubai attack

candidates.summary: A federal court in Texas temporarily blocked the Trump administration from building a border wall and related infrastructure across the Big Bend region. Judge Kathleen Cardone found that the plaintiffs were likely to succeed on at least one claim and faced irreparable harm without an injunction. The planned work is part of a broader $46 billion border-infrastructure program.
candidates.title: Federal court temporarily blocks border-wall construction in Texas Big Bend

candidates.summary: Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth ordered a one-day military stand-down intended to encourage service members to vote, describing the move as apolitical. The announcement followed remarks in which he said military personnel could collectively outvote heavily Democratic cities if all cast ballots.
candidates.title: Hegseth orders one-day military stand-down to encourage voting

candidates.summary: The Navy announced that the USS Abraham Lincoln is scheduled to return to California on October 8 after supporting U.S. operations in the Iran war. Its deployment included more than 260 consecutive days at sea and drew scrutiny over reports of crew stress and shortages of food, medicine and hygiene products.
candidates.title: Navy schedules USS Abraham Lincoln's return after record deployment

candidates.summary: The Kennedy Center said its 2026 Honors ceremony will be held at Washington's Capital One Arena rather than its usual performing-arts complex. The December 7 venue change comes after the center's board voted to close the riverfront building amid a legal dispute over efforts to add President Donald Trump's name to it; no specific explanation for the venue change was given.
candidates.title: Kennedy Center Honors moved to Capital One Arena

candidates.summary: Florida health officials had recorded more than 250 locally acquired dengue cases in 2026, most in Hillsborough County, making the outbreak apparently the largest in the continental United States in decades. Local emergencies were declared in Hillsborough and surrounding counties, and mosquito-control spraying was underway. One Florida dengue death was reported, involving a Tampa woman who died September 4.
candidates.title: Florida dengue outbreak becomes largest in continental U.S. in decades
